page: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 server family. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It operates at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz and is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU configuration includes a 32 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES and SHA_NI.

The instance includes 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. In benchmark evaluations, the D4ads_v6 demonstrates strong single-core performance, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core metrics. Multi-core performance and cryptographic execution fall within the average range. However, memory bandwidth for read-only operations is relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25% for both small and large block sizes.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that require consistent single-thread performance without massive memory bandwidth demands. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, text processing, and lightweight database operations. It is less optimal for memory-bandwidth-intensive tasks, software compilation, or medium-to-large language model inference.
